title: Halden Robotics
description: Warehouse robots that survive a real floor: a seed-stage startup home with sourced traction, named investors, the team and a dated public roadmap.

props.tagline: Seed stage · Bilbao and Rotterdam · 11 people
props.title: Warehouse robots that survive a real floor
props.subtitle: Most autonomous pallet movers are built for clean demos. Ours are built for wet concrete, pallets twenty centimetres off, and the forklift driver who will not slow down for anybody.

image.caption: the robot on a customer floor · 2400×1400

props.title: Four numbers, each with where it came from
props.subtitle: We are eighteen months old. These are the only figures we have, and they are measured rather than estimated.

items.label: Paying deployments
items.description: Two food distribution centres and one parts warehouse. Contracts, not pilots.

items.label: Pallet moves completed
items.description: Fleet controller log, January to August 2026. Forty-one aborted moves in the same period.

items.label: Moves without intervention
items.description: Same log. We publish the intervention count, not only the percentage.

items.label: Seed round, March 2026
items.description: Led by Tramline Ventures, with Kessler Industrial and four angels from the sector.

props.label: What we have not built yet
props.description: No cold-storage certification, no multi-floor handoff, and the fleet API is read-only until Q1. If your site needs any of those this year, we are the wrong supplier — and saying so now is cheaper for both of us.

props.title: One machine, three things it does differently
props.subtitle: We are not building a platform. We build one pallet mover and the controller that runs a fleet of them.

items.title: It expects the floor to be wrong
items.description: Wet patches, missing markings, pallets off-position. It re-plans instead of stopping and paging a human.

items.title: It yields to people, visibly
items.description: A projected floor marking shows where it is going next. Near-miss reports from drivers stopped in week two.

items.title: It runs on the WMS you already have
items.description: Adapters for the three systems our customers use. No rip-and-replace, no eighteen-month integration.
